title: Patrick Stewart’s Many Roles, From ‘Star Trek’ to ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
description: The actor’s long and varied career included Shakespearean roles, “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” comedy and a stint in the Marvel Universe.
author: Claire Moses

title: Patrick Stewart, ‘Star Trek’ Captain and Professor X on ‘X-Men,’ Dies at 86
description: The British actor was 86. He achieved pop-culture stardom as Capt. Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek: The Next Generation.”
author: Anita Gates and William McDonald

title: I Can Hear Everything
description: The world can be tough to navigate with one working ear. Even now with two, I still face challenges.
author: Scott Dodd

title: Trump and His Aides Helped Bolsonaro Flee Brazil and Enter U.S.
description: President Trump ensured Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost a presidential election in Brazil and faces multiple criminal investigations there, could enter the United States, U.S. officials said.
author: Edward Wong, Ana Ionova, Hamed Aleaziz and Tyler Pager

title: Is This the Final Unraveling?
description: What are the key differences between now and two years ago? Between now and 2016?
author: Frank Bruni and Bret Stephens

title: Cabinet Officials on the Campaign Trail? Ethics Experts Say Some Are Breaking the Law.
description: As Trump officials stump for Republican candidates facing difficult races, ethics experts say they are being lax about complying with the Hatch Act, a federal anti-corruption law.
author: Karoun Demirjian

title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Who Helped End One-Party Rule in Mexico, Dies at 92
description: Mr. Cárdenas, the only son of a Mexican president, never won the office but became a leading figure in the country’s democratic transformation.
author: Anthony DePalma

title: RFK Jr. to Allow Broad Use of Unapproved Peptide Injections
description: In a unilateral declaration by the health secretary, several injections promoted by online influencers will become widely available. The F.D.A. had advised against the move.
author: Christina Jewett

title: Ilhan Omar Investigation Involves New Scrutiny of Long-Disputed Marriage
description: Several current and former law enforcement officials said an Obama-era investigation found some evidence that Ms. Omar had entered into a sham marriage with a man suspected of being her brother.
author: Ernesto Londoño

title: After 28 Years Walking the Globe, Karl Bushby Is Almost Home
description: Karl Bushby has walked 31,000 miles, crossing some of the world’s harshest landscapes. He plans to reach his mother’s house in England next week.
author: Jonathan Wolfe

title: How Netanyahu Used Fear, Again, to Win Votes in the Israel Elections
description: Despite years of political baggage, the Israeli prime minister outperformed expectations, and his rivals, by playing on Jewish voters’ fears of Arab political power and potential security threats.
author: David M. Halbfinger

title: Idaho Voters Will Pick Their State Gun on Tuesday
description: An advisory referendum will give Idahoans a choice of six weapons to make their state gun, though none of them are exactly linked to their state.
author: Anna Griffin

title: Mike Beigel, Whose Devices Shaped the Sound of the 70s, Has Died
description: Have a listen. He’s responsible for a funky texture in the 1970s that defined hit songs by Stevie Wonder, the Grateful Dead and many others.
author: Alex Williams

title: Alaska Governor Orders Investigation Into Peltola Campaign Over Second Dan Sullivan Recruitment Claims
description: President Trump had lashed out at Mary Peltola after The New York Times reported that her campaign and national Democrats helped recruit spoiler candidates to the race. He offered no explanation of what crime may have been committed.
author: Kellen Browning and Anna Griffin

title: Europe Is Aflame, and It’s Not Going to Stop
description: The protests roiling the continent express feelings of generational futility.
author: Anton Jäger

title: In Michigan, El-Sayed Faces Heat From Former Primary Rival as Election Nears
description: Representative Haley Stevens has been less than enthusiastic about Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, injecting late intraparty tensions into a race that could decide Senate control.
author: Reid J. Epstein and Tim Balk

title: What Does the Cheesecake Factory’s Designer Think of Obama and Trump’s Jabs at His Décor?
description: Long before its baroque décor and class identity became midterm talking points, this durable restaurant chain survived some withering critiques.
author: Kim Severson

title: Linda McMahon Spends $43,000 on Furniture as She Looks to Close Education Department
description: The education secretary says her old furniture “cannot be configurationally or aesthetically integrated” into new office space.
author: Michael C. Bender

title: Inflation. War. Corruption. Hold Trump Accountable.
description: The American people have a chance to allow the nation to glimpse the end of the Trump era and the start of something brighter.
author: The Editorial Board
